title: AI spending plans and data rules for firms training on Singapore data
asked: Mr Gerald Giam asked what the Government projects spending on its global-leadership and AI-empowered economy strategies, whether it will fund exploratory projects through a Government-owned AI corporation, and whether such entities are more effective than foreign ones where data sovereignty and public interest matter.
response: Mr Tan Kiat How said Singapore's National AI Strategy 2.0 aims to harness AI for the public good, with investment across the public and private sectors, capability-building in research, government and industry, and real-world applications. He said decisions weigh Singapore's needs alongside performance, security, resilience and cost-effectiveness, with due regard for data security and the public interest, and that Singapore uses local capabilities while partnering international entities that can impart knowledge, build skills and create local jobs. He pointed to the upcoming 2026 Budget Statement and Committee of Supply debates for details on developing an AI-empowered economy. On the supplementary, he said all organisations must comply with the Personal Data Protection Act, including the Transfer Limitation Obligation when data goes overseas, and that public sector data can only be shared where there is a legitimate public-interest purpose with ministerial authorisation and contractual safeguards in place.

key_points.point: The Government's stated aim under National AI Strategy 2.0 is to use AI for the public good and improve Singaporeans' lives.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Under Singapore's National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy 2.0, we seek to harness AI for the public good and to improve the lives of Singaporeans.

key_points.point: Capability decisions weigh Singapore's needs against performance, security, resilience and cost-effectiveness of the technology.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: we consider what serves Singapore's needs, alongside other factors, such as the performance, security, resilience and cost-effectiveness of the technology

key_points.point: Singapore uses local capabilities and partners with international entities, including leading companies that impart knowledge, build skills and create local jobs.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: We leverage local capabilities and partner with international entities, including leading companies who can impart knowledge, build skills and create local jobs.

key_points.point: Details of how Singapore will develop an AI-empowered economy will come in the 2026 Budget Statement and Committee of Supply debates.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: The Member may refer to the upcoming 2026 Budget Statement and the Committee of Supply debates for more details on how Singapore will develop an AI-empowered economy.

key_points.point: All organisations must meet their obligations under the Personal Data Protection Act.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: all organisations must comply with their obligations under the Personal Data Protection Act

key_points.point: The Transfer Limitation Obligation applies when data is transferred to another country, including for training AI models.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: the Transfer Limitation Obligation, which applies when data is transferred to another country

key_points.point: Public sector data can be shared only where there is a legitimate purpose supporting the public interest, with ministerial authorisation and contractual data protection and security agreements in place.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Such data can only be shared, and that is for the public sector data that the Member has mentioned if there is a legitimate purpose to support the public interest

key_points.point: Questions on the commercial or business model have to be use-case specific and driven by the relevant agencies.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: His other questions around the specifics of the commercial model, the business model, these have to be use case specific and driven by the use case problems and the relevant agencies looking after it.

left_open: The projected expenditure figures for the global-leadership and AI-empowered economy strategies.
Whether the Government will fund exploratory projects with breakout growth potential through a Government-owned AI corporation.
Whether Government-owned entities are considered more effective than foreign entities where data sovereignty and public interest are paramount.

Whether foreign firms using Singapore public data sets for AI training would be required to commit to a structured local knowledge transfer programme and share a portion of resulting intellectual property with Singaporean firms.
Whether commercial AI developers, particularly foreign-based ones, would be charged a fee for training models on public data sets, and how such revenue would be accounted for and publicised.
supplementary: Data protection safeguards and commercial models for foreign firms training AI on Singapore data.
